instrument_name: Wisconsin Publication W-166 Withholding Tax Guide (1/26) - read locally
article_or_section: Supplemental wage payments; Reciprocity; Special Minnesota arrangement; Alternate method
figure_or_rule_carried: Supplemental wages: with regular wages as one payment, or flat percentages on estimated annual gross: 0-12,760 3.54%; 12,760-25,520 4.65%; 25,520-280,950 5.30%; 280,950+ 7.65%. Reciprocity: IL, IN, KY, MI (employer not required to withhold WI; written verification, Form W-220). WI resident working in MN: special arrangement, no WI withholding if MN withholds. Own certificate WT-4 (federal W-4 not usable). Alternate method: single deduction 6,702 below 17,780 gross, phase-out 12% to 0 at 73,630; married 9,461 below 25,727, 20% to 0 at 73,032; exemption 400 each. Caveat: guide cover says withholding periods on or after 2022-01-01 and news box says rates continue for 2025; no 2026-specific table change printed. No rounding rule or local-tax text found in the 63 pages.

instrument_name: UCT-8291-E Employer Power of Attorney Assignment (DWD forms page)
figure_or_rule_carried: Form used by employers to assign an agent full power to represent them before the Wisconsin UI Division. Employer Service Provider filing page (dwd.wisconsin.gov/uitax/serv-providers.htm) seen only as a search lead, not read.

First 14,000 of wages paid to each employee (calendar year 2013 and beyond) is taxed; wages above are reported but not taxed. Quarterly reports due by close of month following quarter end, filed even with no payroll. Chapter 108 Wis. Stats. Employee contribution: handbook describes only employer payroll-tax funding; no employee deduction statement located (absence not proven).

instrument_name: Seattle payroll expense tax page (SMC 5.38) - City Finance
authority: City of Seattle Office of City Finance
figure_or_rule_carried: Local payroll-based tax in WA is an employer business tax on payroll expense, not withheld from employee wages: 2026 applies to businesses with 9,074,409 or more Seattle payroll expense in 2025 and at least one employee with 194,452 or more annual compensation in 2026; quarterly returns (first due 2026-04-30, Q4 packet due 2027-01-31); payroll processing companies remitting for clients submit a Taxpayer Authorization Form per client unless filing in FileLocal. FAQ question whether it is a tax on the employee is listed but its answer text was not expanded.

instrument_name: RCW 39.12.020 Prevailing rate of wage on public works
figure_or_rule_carried: Hourly wages on public works and public building service maintenance contracts of the state or any county, municipality or political subdivision shall be not less than the prevailing rate of wage for an hour of work in the same trade in the locality; contracts over 10,000 require posting of a statement of intent. Administering agency: Department of Labor and Industries prevailing wage section (L&I page read via WebFetch).

Employer withholds if wages are expected to equal 1,000 or more during the year; tables and rules from the Department of Revenue; the employer may compute wages to the nearest dollar when determining the amount withheld (rounding rule).

instrument_name: SCDOR WH-1603F (Rev. 11/4/25) Formula for computing SC 2026 withholding - read locally
figure_or_rule_carried: Confirms US-SC-007: allowance 5,000; standard deduction 10% of gross max 7,500 with 1+ allowances (none with zero); subtraction method 0% below 3,640, 3% less 109.20 to 18,230, 6% less 656.10 above; addition method 6% plus 437.70; worked example 750 weekly 3 allowances = 549.90 yearly = 10.58 weekly. File has no supplemental/bonus method.

instrument_name: SCDOR WH-105 Withholding Tax Information Guide (Rev. 2/13/23)
figure_or_rule_carried: SC resident working in another state: tax withheld for the other state; if that state has no income tax, SC tax must be withheld (state of legal residence). Employees hired after 2019-12-31 without SC W-4: withhold at zero allowances. Nonresident employers pay quarterly/monthly (500 threshold). Guide does not mention reciprocity agreements, supplemental-wage rules, local wage tax or a POA form.

instrument_name: SC Code 41-10-30 itemized statement of pay (chapter 41-10)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer shall furnish each employee an itemized statement of gross pay and deductions made for each pay period. Chapter 41-10 (payment of wages) has no prevailing-wage section (absence limited to this chapter).

Supplemental payment not concurrent with a payroll period: withhold 6.25 percent as if no allowance claimed. If wages exceed the highest bracket the employer may elect to compute wages to the nearest dollar (rounding).

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268B.14 Paid Leave premium (statute text via summarizer)
figure_or_rule_carried: Summarizer reading: standard employers total premium 0.7 percent of taxable wages (0.4 medical only / 0.3 family only with private plan); employer pays at least 50 percent, employee the rest by wage deduction; small employers 75 percent of the rate with employer minimum 25 percent; wage cap = Social Security wage base. instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 268.035 taxable wages and 268.051 tax payment
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxable wages = wages in covered employment per calendar year up to 60 percent of the state average annual wage rounded to nearest 1,000 (the 2026 dollar figure was NOT read; uimn.org page not loadable and not archived). UI tax paid quarterly by the employer at its assigned rate; no deduction from wages authorised in the section. New taxpaying employer rate = average industry experience rating plus base rate and assessments, not less than 1 percent; industry by NAICS two digits (construction five).
Minnesota has a state prevailing wage law for public building projects funded wholly or partly by state funds; administered by the Department of Labor and Industry (chapter 177).

instrument_name: Arizona Form A-4 employer instructions (2026) - read locally
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding is a percentage of gross taxable wages (box 1 W-2 definition); new employee completes A-4 within 5 days, else default 2.0 percent; zero-percent election renewed annually (new A-4 by 2/15); no withholding for nonresidents present under 60 days a year (related-entity test); extra amount election; nonresident in AZ 60+ days must have withholding.

Percentage options 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5 percent of gross taxable wages. Nonresident exempt from AZ withholding with Form WEC if resident of California, Indiana, Oregon or Virginia and entitled to credit on Form 140NR. Nonresident working in AZ: withholding required after 60 days (earlier by agreement). AZ residents working outside AZ may request voluntary withholding with Form A-4V. Registration for withholding (ADOR) and UI (DES) via JT-1. Statutes listed: A.R.S. 43-401 to 43-435; A.A.C. R15-2B-101/102. Page has no local wage tax, supplemental-rate, rounding or POA text.

instrument_name: A.R.S. 43-401 Withholding tax; rates; election by employee
figure_or_rule_carried: At payment of wages, salary, bonus or other emolument for services performed in AZ the employer deducts an amount prescribed by tables adopted by the department; no rounding rule in the opening paragraphs read (remainder of section not read).

Direct deposit or payroll-card payment: employee shall be furnished a written or electronic statement of earnings and withholdings (no content list). 23-364(D): business name/address/phone in writing at hire; payroll records of hours, wages and earned paid sick time kept four years; notices posted. Paydays at least twice a month, not more than 16 days apart.

Commission keeps a separate account per employer credited with contributions paid by the employer; section mentions no employee contribution (employer-only inference, section-limited; not an explicit prohibition).
